Change the order of integration in the integral
[MATH: \displaystyle
\int_0^1 \int_0^{2} \int_0^{\sqrt[3]{z}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z]
so that it is integrated first with respect to [MATH: z,] then over a region [MATH: D] in the [MATH: xy]-plane. The integration region [MATH: R] is shown above.

sections.normalized_html:
We wish to find the limits of integration [MATH: u_1(x,y)] and [MATH: u_2(x,y)] such that

[MATH: \int_0^1 \int_0^{2} \int_0^{\sqrt[3]{z}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z = \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\right] \textrm{d}A.]

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration [MATH: R] can be written as a type III region as follows:

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \:\: {:} \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt[3]{z} \big\}]

To change the order of integration from [MATH: \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z] to [MATH: \textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}A,] we write [MATH: R] as a type I region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the [MATH: z]-axis and in the direction of increasing [MATH: z,] as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

  • The bottom boundary of the region, written in the form [MATH: z=z(x,y),] is [MATH: y = \sqrt[3]{z}, \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z = y^3.]

  • The top boundary of the region is [MATH: z = 1.]

Therefore, the type I representation of [MATH: R] is

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \:\: {:} \:\: (x,y) \in D, \:\: y^3\leq z \leq 1 \big\},]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to [MATH: z] and then over [MATH: D,] we obtain

[MATH: \int_0^1 \int_0^{2} \int_0^{\sqrt[3]{z}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z = \iint\limits_D \left[\int_{y^3}^{1} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\right] \textrm{d}A.]
